recipes.name: Spaghetti all'Amatriciana inspired by Eat Pray Love
ingredients: 1 tbsp kosher salt + more to taste
1 1/2 oz pecorino romano, grated + more to garnish
To taste freshly ground black pepper
11 oz semolina flour + more for dusting
To taste freshly ground black pepper
4 oz guanciale, cut into thin strips
1 whole calabrian chili, stem removed + chopped
1 tbsp kosher salt + more to taste
To taste freshly ground black pepper
instructions: For the Simple Amatriciana

Add the guanciale to a large cold skillet. Begin heating the pan over medium-low heat and cook the guanciale until the fat has rendered out, about 8-10 minutes. If the guanciale begins to smoke, add ¼ cup of water to the pan. - 4 oz guanciale cut into lardons

Add the tomatoes and red chili to the skillet. Cook the sauce, while stirring periodically, for 10-12 minutes or until thickened. Optionally, remove the chili before adding the cooked pasta. - 8 oz pureed tomatoes - 1 fresh red chili
Meanwhile, bring a pot of water to a boil, then season with salt. - 1 tbsp kosher salt + more to taste

Add the dried pasta to the boiling and cook for about 1 minute less than the box instructions for al dente pasta. Using tongs, transfer the cooked pasta to the large skillet with the tomato sauce. Reserve the cooking water. - 8 oz dried spaghetti
Add about ½ cup of cooking water to the skillet, then stir/toss to combine the sauce with the pasta. Cook the mixture, while stirring, for about 1-2 minutes longer or until the pasta is al dente.

Turn off the heat and stir in the pecorino cheese, adding more cooking water as necessary to thin out the sauce. Season the pasta to taste with salt and pepper. If the cheese doesn’t melt entirely, reheat the sauce over a pot of simmering water. - 1 ½ oz pecorino romano grated + more to garnish - To taste freshly ground black pepper - kosher salt + more to taste
Serve immediately and garnish with more pecorino as desired. - pecorino romano grated + more to garnish
For the Fresh Pasta Dough
Add 10 ounces of semolina flour to a clean work surface. Form a shallow and wide well in the center of the flour, then add the eggs. - 11 oz semolina flour + more for dusting - 6 oz eggs
Using a fork, whisk the eggs in the center of the well until homogenous. Slowly begin to incorporate flour from the exterior walls of the flour well.
Once a pancake batter consistency is reached inside of the well or the sides of the well have collapsed, use a bench scraper to incorporate the remaining flour.
Knead the pasta dough until a homogenous dough forms and no dry spots of flour remain. If the dough is sticky, add another 1-2 ounces of semolina flour.

Working with one portion at a time, feed the pasta dough into a spaghetti extruding feeder; alternatively roll the dough out using the pasta roller, then cut the dough sheet using a spaghetti cutter attachment.
Repeat with the remaining dough. Transfer the extruded/cut pasta to a sheet tray dusted with more semolina flour.
For the One Pot Amatriciana
Add the pancetta to a large cold skillet. Begin heating the skillet over medium-low heat and cook until most of the fat has rendered out of the pancetta, about 4-6 minutes. - 4 oz pancetta cubed
Add the tomatoes and red chili flakes to the skillet, then cook for 10 minutes or until thickened to the point of looking dry. - 8 oz crushed tomatoes - ½ tsp crushed red chili flakes
Add the water to the skillet and bring to a simmer. Then add the dried spaghetti to the pot and cover. - 12 oz water - 8 oz dried spaghetti
Cook the pasta 2-3 minutes longer than box instructions for al dente pasta. Make sure to stir the pasta periodically. Add another ¼ cup of water at a time if the mixture becomes too dry.

Once the pasta is al dente, turn off the heat and stir in the pecorino cheese. Season the pasta to taste with salt and pepper, then serve immediately. - 1 ½ oz pecorino romano grated - To taste kosher salt - To taste freshly ground black pepper
For the Babish Amatriciana

Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Meanwhile, cut two shallow cross hatches into the bottom of each tomato. Add the tomatoes to the boiling water and cook for 30 seconds. Using tongs or a metal spider, transfer the par-boiled tomatoes to an ice bath. - 4 ripe tomatoes

Once chilled, peel the skin off of the tomatoes, then cut the tomatoes in half. Scrape out the seeds and pulp, then set them aside in a bowl. Dice the remaining tomatoe flesh and place them in a separate bowl. Strain the reserved tomatoe pulp/seeds into the diced tomatoes, then discard the seeds.

Add the guanciale to a large cold skillet. Begin heating the skillet over medium-low heat and cook the guanciale until most of the fat has rendered out, about 8-10 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove the cooked guanciale, leaving the rendered fat in the skillet. - 4 oz guanciale cut into thin strips

Add the onion and cook until translucent, 3-5 minutes. Then, add the chopped calabrian chili and cook for 30 seconds to 1 minute or until fragrant. - ½ small yellow onion chopped - 1 clove garlic minced - 1 whole calabrian chili stem removed + chopped
Deglaze the pan with the wine and cook for 1 minute or until the alcohol burns off. Make sure to scrape the fond off the bottom of the pan using a wooden spoon or spatula. - 60 ml dry white wine
Add the 1 cup of the chopped tomato mixture and the tomato puree to the skillet. Cook the sauce, while stirring periodically, for 10-12 minutes or until thickened. - 6 oz tomato puree
Meanwhile, bring a pot of water to a boil, then season with salt. - 1 tbsp kosher salt + more to taste

Add the fresh pasta to the boiling and cook until al dente, about 2 minutes. Using tongs, transfer the cooked pasta to the large skillet with the tomato sauce. Reserve the cooking water. - 8 oz fresh spaghetti
Add about ½ cup of cooking water to the skillet, then stir/toss to combine the sauce with the pasta.

Turn off the heat and stir in the pecorino cheese, reserved guanciale, and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. Season the pasta to taste with salt and pepper. - 1 ½ oz pecorino romano grated - To taste freshly ground black pepper - Extra virgin olive oil - To garnish: basil leaves
Serve immediately and garnish with a sprig of basil leaves.
